## Purpose

The application shell: `AppHeader` (top nav, running-pipeline badge/dropdown, notification bell, profile
menu) and `DashboardLayout`.

**`DashboardLayout` is the composition root** — it owns `mainView` routing and mounts every dashboard-era
page: home, library, history, settings, analytics, saved workflows, the workflow composer, and the live
execution screen. Nearly every other `components/*` page module is depended on by this one.

## Shape

- [AppHeader.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/layout/AppHeader.tsx) — pure presentational nav bar. Takes `currentPage`/`onNavigate` plus live-run props
  (`recentRuns`, `activePipelineRunId`, `runAgentsCompletedMap`) and derives the single-run badge or
  multi-run dropdown from them; the profile dropdown routes to settings/analytics/history via
  `onNavigate`. No data fetching of its own.

- [DashboardLayout.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/layout/DashboardLayout.tsx) — the large stateful root. Holds `mainView`
  (`"home" | "library" | "history" | "settings" | "analytics" | "input" | "execution" | "catalog" |
  "saved-workflows" | "composer"`) and switches on it near the bottom of the render to mount the
  matching page component (`HomeLaunchGrid`, `LibraryPage`, `WorkflowHistory`, `AccountSettings`,
  `AnalyticsPage`, `SavedWorkflowsPage`, `RunChatLane` + `PreviewPanel` for execution, etc.) under a
  shared `AppHeader`. It owns:
  - pipeline-run notification/toast bookkeeping (mapping SSE/WS pipeline events to the
    `useNotifications` store)
  - the revision-launch handlers (`handleRevisePpt`/`handleReviseUserStory`/`handleRevisePrototype`/
    `handleRevisePrototypeV2`/`handleReviseBacklog`/`handleReviseAppBuilder`/`handleReviseCustom`); the v2
    and backlog ones post to the revisions endpoint (v2 picks the Fast or Depth pipeline; backlog is
    dispatched before the prototype branch, whose content fallback would otherwise catch it)
  - the back origin: the Runs list and the dashboard record themselves (`rememberBackOrigin`), and
    a run's Back pops to that list (`backToOrigin`, both in [lib/navigation.ts](../../frontend/src/lib/navigation.ts))
  - the questionnaire/gate wiring passed down to the execution view

  It consumes `useRunConnection` (SSE transport), `useNotifications`, and `SkillsHooksContext`.

- **`mainView` vs the URL (spec 015-frontend-routing)**: `mainView` is set two ways — optimistically
  by a click handler (e.g. `setMainView("input")` before `router.push`), and synced from
  `[...view]/page.tsx`'s `initialMainViewFor(parsedView)` on cold mount/back-forward via a
  `useEffect` that overwrites `mainView` whenever `initialMainView` is truthy and differs from the
  current value. A route whose parsed screen maps to a DIFFERENT known `MainView` will stomp an
  optimistic set made just before the `router.push` — `createRouteForType` exists specifically to
  route dynamic-catalog pipeline types to a URL that avoids this (a bare fallback route parsed to a
  truthy, wrong `MainView` and silently no-op'd the click).

- `*.test.tsx` files cover accessibility (`AppHeader.a11y`) and layout-specific regression fixes
  (`catalogHome`, `fix194`, `laneTitle`, `launchLatch`, `revisionRouting`).

## Why this shape

`DashboardLayout` is the **historical single composition root** for the whole dashboard — every
page-level module funnels through its `mainView` switch rather than each owning its own route, which
is why its import list spans nearly all other `components/*` directories.

The size and the dense inline comments (many tagged with `FIX-`/`ISS-`/`BUG-` ids) reflect that it has
absorbed most cross-cutting concerns — concurrent-run notification ownership, SSE reconnect replay,
revision-family linkage — that would otherwise need their own coordination layer. **It is a module that
accretes fixes rather than one that was designed flat.**
